html:
Caguana, in the mountains near Utuado in Puerto Rico, is a Taino ceremonial centre built around 1270 CE, with ball courts and plazas lined with carved stones. It is among the most important Taino sites in the Caribbean.

The Taino played a sacred ball game called batey here and held ceremonies called areitos with song and dance. Petroglyphs on the stones show faces and figures, perhaps spirits or ancestors, the zemis.

The site shows the Taino of Boriken, the old name of Puerto Rico, at the height of their culture, about two centuries before Ponce de Leon arrived. It was excavated in the 20th century and is now a park. Many Puerto Ricans see in it the roots of their identity, along with the Saladoid peoples before them.
